answer.question: Are we on pace to hit goal, and where do we land by election day if nothing changes?
answer.answer:
Yes on the year-to-date pace (103.3% of goal to date), but no on the election-day projection — at the current rate the program lands about 3,303 doors short of the 60,632 goal.

- Program total, to date Sep 21–Oct 18: 33,503 doors against 32,431 goal to date, 103.3% [view:v_office_pace_total]
- Projection: 57,329 doors by Nov 3 (94.6% of goal), a shortfall of 3,303; last 7 days averaged 1,489.1 doors/day with 16 knocking days left [view:v_office_pace_total]
- Northside: 13,647 doors, 112.5% of goal to date; projected 23,583 vs a 22,675 goal, so 908 doors over [view:v_office_pace]
- Harbor: 11,351 doors, 105.3% of goal to date; projected 19,150 vs a 20,157 goal, 1,007 short (95% of goal) [view:v_office_pace]
- Eastgate: 8,505 doors, only 89.3% of goal to date; projected 14,596 vs a 17,800 goal, 3,204 short (82% of goal) [view:v_office_pace]
- Shifts to close the gap: 33.3 shifts/day needed program-wide vs 29.3/day now, i.e. 4.1 extra shifts per day; Northside needs none, Harbor 1.3 and Eastgate 4.4 more per day [view:v_office_pace_total, view:v_office_pace]
- The projection assumes nothing changes: doors to date plus the last 7 days' average daily doors times the 16 knocking days left (Oct 19–Nov 3) [doc:program-plan#pace-and-projection]

cases.question: What counts as flash knocking under our QC rules?

answer.question: What counts as flash knocking under our QC rules?
answer.answer:
Flash knocking is recording doors faster than a person could realistically walk to and knock them.

- A shift is flagged when 10 or more consecutive knocks are recorded less than 30 seconds apart [doc:qc-rules#flash-knocking]
- Confirmed flash knocking is rolled back: the knocks in that window no longer count as doors or contacts, though they stay in the data with rolled_back = true [doc:counting-doors#rollbacks]
- A whole shift recorded this way is rolled back in full [doc:qc-rules#flash-knocking]
- Every open flash-knocking flag needs a conversation between the field lead and the canvasser before the canvasser's next shift; two or more flash-knocking or householding flags in one week for the same canvasser go to the field director [doc:qc-rules#what-happens-after-a-flag]

sources.text: Flash knocking is recording doors faster than a person can walk to them and knock. A shift is flagged when 10 or more consecutive knocks are recorded less than 30 seconds apart. Confirmed flash knocking is rolled back: the knocks in the window no longer count as doors or contacts. A whole shift recorded this way is rolled back in full.

When QC confirms flash knocking, the knocks in the flagged window are rolled back: they stay in the data with rolled_back = true but are removed from doors and contacts. Rollbacks happen after the day's client report has been pulled, so they never change a report that was already sent.

Every open flag needs a conversation between the field lead and the canvasser before the canvasser's next shift, using the timestamped evidence on the flag. After the conversation the flag is marked reviewed. Two or more householding or flash knocking flags in one week for the same canvasser go to the field director.

sources.text: Cost per door is GOTV wages (paid hours times the hourly rate for the person's role) divided by doors for the same office and period. Overtime premiums are left out of this figure.

A new office should sit closest to the doors we still need: the untouched doors in our turf, weighted by how many doors each precinct has left. Untouched or lightly touched precincts (under 25 percent of doors touched) that are dense (over 2,000 doors per square mile) are worth a new office; sparse precincts (under 1,000 doors per square mile) are slow to knock and are better handled at the end with drive-out shifts. Candidate sites are listed in the candidate office sites table.
